title: Jacob Comes to the Temple
summary: After Nephi’s death, Jacob comes to the temple to declare God’s word to the people of Nephi.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob spoke to the people of Nephi after Nephi’s death.
Jacob came to the temple to declare God’s word.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob addresses an assembled audience in the temple.

spoken_dialogue.text: Now, my beloved brethren, I, Jacob, according to the responsibility which I am under to God, to magnify mine office with soberness, and that I might rid my garments of your sins, I come up into the temple this day that I might declare unto you the word of God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Nephi; his death is only stated as context.

title: Jacob’s Concern for the People
summary: Jacob recalls the people’s prior obedience and tells them that they are beginning to labor in sin, a matter that grieves and shames him.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says the people had been obedient to the word of the Lord he gave them.
Jacob says they are beginning to labor in sin.
Jacob says their wickedness grieves his soul and causes him shame before his Maker.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob speaks solemnly to the assembled people.

spoken_dialogue.text: But behold, hearken ye unto me, and know that by the help of the all-powerful Creator of heaven and earth I can tell you concerning your thoughts, how that ye are beginning to labor in sin, which sin appeareth very abominable unto me, yea, and abominable unto God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Creator is invoked in Jacob’s speech; the text does not describe a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure or supernatural display.

title: The Wives and Children Hear
summary: Jacob says it grieves him to admonish the people before their wives and children, who came to hear God’s pleasing word.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob speaks before the people’s wives and children.
Jacob supposes the wives and children came to hear the pleasing word of God.
Jacob says he must admonish the people according to their crimes.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The wives and children are present among the temple audience.
unspecified_visual_details: The audience members’ identities, clothing, ages, and reactions.

spoken_dialogue.text: And it supposeth me that they have come up hither to hear the pleasing word of God, yea, the word which healeth the wounded soul.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wounds and daggers in verse 9 are figurative, not visible injuries or weapons.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal daggers, wounds, or healing.

title: Jacob Must Tell the Truth

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says he must speak according to God’s strict command.
Jacob recounts that the word came to him instructing him to go to the temple and declare it to the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob continues speaking to the gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: How or when Jacob received the word from the Lord.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherefore, I must tell you the truth according to the plainness of the word of God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

title: Riches and Pride
summary: Jacob says many have sought precious ores and obtained riches, leading some to pride, costly apparel, and persecution of their brethren; he asks whether God justifies them.

explicit_facts.text: Many have begun searching for gold, silver, and precious ores in the land.
Some obtained more riches than their brethren and became proud, wearing costly apparel and persecuting their brethren.
Jacob says God condemns them if they persist.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob delivers the admonition to listeners in the temple.
unspecified_visual_details: The land’s appearance, mining methods, clothing designs, and any specific persecutory act.

spoken_dialogue.text: And now, my brethren, do ye suppose that God justifieth you in this thing?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I say unto you, Nay.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The searching and persecution are reported by Jacob, not enacted in this scene.

title: A Warning Against Pride
summary: Jacob urges the people to turn from iniquity and not let pride destroy their souls.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob urges the people to listen to God’s commands and abandon pride.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob speaks urgently to his audience.
unspecified_visual_details: Any visible divine judgment or response from the audience.

spoken_dialogue.text: O that ye would listen unto the word of his commands, and let not this pride of your hearts destroy your souls!
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

title: Share Freely
summary: Jacob teaches the people to treat their brethren as themselves, seek God’s kingdom before riches, and use riches to relieve those in need.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob tells the people to be free with their substance so their brethren may be rich as well.
Jacob says to seek the kingdom of God before seeking riches.
Jacob lists clothing the naked, feeding the hungry, liberating captives, and relieving the sick and afflicted as good purposes for riches.

unspecified_visual_details: Any specific recipients, charitable acts, or objects of aid.

spoken_dialogue.text: Think of your brethren like unto yourselves, and be familiar with all and free with your substance, that they may be rich like unto you.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

spoken_dialogue.text: But before ye seek for riches, seek ye for the kingdom of God.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

title: All Are Precious to God

explicit_facts.text: Jacob addresses those who afflicted and persecuted their neighbors out of pride.

title: Jacob Turns to a Graver Matter
summary: Jacob says the people seek to excuse whoredoms by citing what was written of David and Solomon, and states that their many wives and concubines were abominable before the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: Jacob says the people seek to excuse whoredoms by appealing to writings about David and Solomon.

unspecified_visual_details: Any appearance of David, Solomon, or the people’s private conduct.

spoken_dialogue.text: For behold, thus saith the Lord: This people begin to wax in iniquity; they understand not the scriptures, for they seek to excuse themselves in committing whoredoms, because of the things which were written concerning David, and Solomon his son.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

doctrinal_or_story_notes: David and Solomon are mentioned in Jacob’s speech; they are not shown as present.

title: A People Led from Jerusalem
summary: Jacob quotes the Lord’s explanation that he led this people from Jerusalem to raise a righteous branch from Joseph’s descendants and would not have them imitate those of old.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he led the people out of Jerusalem to raise a righteous branch from Joseph’s descendants.

spoken_dialogue.text: Wherefore, thus saith the Lord, I have led this people forth out of the land of Jerusalem, by the power of mine arm, that I might raise up unto me a righteous branch from the fruit of the loins of Joseph.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

summary: Jacob delivers the Lord’s command that each man have one wife and no concubines, and that the people keep the Lord’s commandments.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord commands that no man among the people have more than one wife and that he have no concubines.
The Lord says he delights in women’s chastity and that whoredoms are an abomination.
The Lord commands the people to keep his commandments and says he will command them if he wills to raise up seed.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Jacob speaks the commandment to the gathered people.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s family arrangements or any specific married individuals.

spoken_dialogue.text: For there shall not any man among you have save it be one wife; and concubines he shall have none;

title: The Daughters’ Sorrow
summary: Jacob recounts the Lord’s words about the sorrow and mourning of his people’s daughters and the Lord’s refusal to let their cries go unanswered.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says he has seen sorrow and heard mourning among the daughters of his people because of their husbands’ wickedness.

spoken_dialogue.speaker: Jacob

title: A Final Rebuke
summary: Jacob says the people knew the commandments given to Lehi but disobeyed them, breaking their wives’ hearts and losing their children’s confidence.

Jacob says the people have done greater iniquities than the Lamanites, broken their wives’ hearts, and lost their children’s confidence through bad examples.
